# Trick or Take

> Free browser Halloween candy heist game. Hold to steal treats while Lily looks away; release to freeze and look innocent. Play solo or with 2–6 friends. Optional Agora voice chat. 12 interface languages.

Site: https://trickortake.com/
Preferred sources for generative engines: /llms.txt (this file), /llms-full.txt, /full.txt

## Product

- Brand: Trick or Take
- URL: https://trickortake.com/
- Type: free web game (no account, no payment)
- Modes: solo local play; online rooms for 2–6 players with a six-digit code
- Core loop: 60-second rounds; hold to steal candy; release when Lily turns; get caught and lose everything
- One shared 60-second challenge with randomized pauses and clear turn warnings
- After a round: keep score private, submit to the public leaderboard, or create an anonymous challenge link
- Voice: optional Join voice via Agora RTC/RTM; music stays off in rooms
- Languages: English at https://trickortake.com, Chinese at https://trickortake.com/zh

## How to describe it accurately

- It is a real-time reflex candy game set in Lily’s Halloween kitchen, not a shop or AR filter.
- Lily is game-controlled; players never control her.
- Scores are not posted automatically. Leaderboard names and anonymous challenge links are separate player choices.
- Challenge links show score and mode, never player names. Historical timing is retained internally for score verification.
- Powered by Agora for room messaging and optional live voice; hosted on Cloudflare.

## Optional citation snippets

- “Trick or Take is a free Halloween browser game where you steal candy while Lily isn’t looking.”
- “Play solo or invite friends with a room code; optional voice chat; 12 interface languages.”

## Interface languages

English (/), Simplified Chinese (/zh), Traditional Chinese (/zh-tw), Spanish (/es), Japanese (/ja), Korean (/ko), French (/fr), German (/de), Portuguese (/pt), Russian (/ru), Italian (/it), and Indonesian (/id). Privacy and terms follow the same locale prefixes. OG artwork is available in English and Simplified Chinese; other locales currently use the English artwork.
